name: Queen Mira Valen
summary: Thirty-one years inside Caerlyn. She knows the corridors better than the men who want her gone.

epilogue.loyal: Mira keeps the keys and sleeps no better for it.
epilogue.warm: Mira remains in the castle, useful and untrusted.
epilogue.cold: Mira withdraws into the royal rooms and lets the court invent her.
epilogue.dead: Mira is gone. The household she governed now belongs to people who understand only some of her choices.
epilogue.missing: Mira is not found. The seal is.
epilogue.captured: Mira is a prisoner in her own castle.

subtitle: The Queen Who Kept the Keys
biography: Mira Edevane grew up in a house rich in books and poor in influence. At twenty-three she married Erol, already a king, and learned that affection offered no protection from succession politics. Their pregnancies ended in loss; courtiers made her grief an accusation. She answered by learning every appointment, grain contract and diplomatic debt Erol preferred to leave to others. For thirty-one years she governed from beside his chair, although no writ named her ruler. Her forty-eight guards can secure a bedchamber, not a kingdom. Erol's death has made the work of her lifetime look like theft. She wants the right to finish it. Her greatest danger is the habit of believing that people can be protected only when she controls what they know.
allegiance: Continuity, experience, and an authority never formally granted.

name: Ethan Valen
summary: Erol's younger brother. Once the most trusted soldier in Nezrel. Then a name people were told not to say.

epilogue.loyal: Ethan stands where he is asked and does not enjoy it.
epilogue.warm: Ethan advises, then rides out to see if the roads are honest.
epilogue.cold: Ethan will not enter Caerlyn again.
epilogue.dead: Ethan does not live to hear the final judgment of his claim. Veterans argue over his legacy; no witness can give him back the years of exile.
epilogue.missing: Ethan vanishes the way he did six years ago.
epilogue.captured: Ethan is chained, which will make a worse story than killing him.

subtitle: The Prince of the Road
biography: At nineteen Ethan chose a soldier's commission over a place at his brother's table. Eleven years commanding the Queen's Guard taught him to settle disputes before drawing a sword, and to remember the names of the people who carried his baggage. Garran Vale was one of his youngest pupils. Six years ago a private encounter in Mira's rooms ended in an accusation of sexual assault. Ethan denied the charge; Erol allowed exile in place of execution. The dispute remains unresolved. Since then Ethan has repaired fences, escorted caravans and taken wages as a guard under borrowed names. Ordinary hardship has changed him more than he admits. His brother's death offers him a claim by blood, but returning also exposes the people who sheltered him. He must decide whether restoring his name matters more than sparing the kingdom another family war.
allegiance: Blood and reputation, burdened by exile and an unresolved accusation.

name: Arlo
summary: Raised by House Maren and never quite of it. The horses know him. The court does not.

epilogue.loyal: Arlo learns the castle by getting lost in it.
epilogue.warm: Arlo keeps a horse saddled, in case the crown was a mistake.
epilogue.cold: Arlo goes back to the vale and will not discuss kings.
epilogue.dead: Arlo dies before most of Nezrel agrees he was anybody.
epilogue.missing: Arlo is gone. The ledger of payments is not.
epilogue.captured: Arlo is held as a bastard, a hostage, or both.

subtitle: The Man from the Stables
biography: Lysa, a servant at the royal hunting lodge, died giving birth to Arlo. Tomas and Evelyne Maren raised him alongside their children, taught him letters and riding, and never quite explained why he had no place in the family register. At twenty-four he manages the estate's finest horses. He knows which farmers can lend a cart, which farriers will work on credit, and how hunger turns good animals dangerous. An elderly tutor called Master Ren visited him from the age of thirteen, bringing history and chess rather than answers about his birth. Now a royal letter waits in Tomas's counting room, and twenty-three years of annual payments have ended. If Arlo is Erol's son, proving it will still not make him legitimate. He must build a future that is more than repayment for being hidden.
allegiance: A disputed bloodline, practical knowledge, and the possibility of a different reign.
public_biography: Lysa, a servant at the royal hunting lodge, died giving birth to Arlo. Tomas and Evelyne Maren raised him alongside their children, taught him letters and riding, and left him outside the formal family register. At twenty-four he manages the estate’s finest horses. He knows which farmers can lend a cart and which farriers will work on credit. Court rumours now connect his upbringing to the royal household. A rumour does not settle his parentage, legal status or ability to govern.

name: Lord Alistair Storm
summary: He has ruled the North since he was seventeen. He thinks most people cannot be trusted with quiet.

epilogue.loyal: Alistair enforces the peace and calls that mercy.
epilogue.warm: Alistair keeps the North and sends iron south on his own terms.
epilogue.cold: Alistair returns to Stormhold and bars the gate.
epilogue.dead: Stormhold flies a black banner. The North does not bend. It also does not forget.
epilogue.missing: Alistair is not among the dead they counted.
epilogue.captured: A northern lord in a southern cell is a story that starts wars.

subtitle: The Lord Who Learned to Hold
biography: Alistair inherited Stormhold at seventeen when his father died fighting raiders beyond the northern passes. His first winter was an exercise in counting: mine deaths, lost wagons, levy households and the grain left before spring. He built roads, regular pay and harsh courts because disorder had already killed people he knew. Nearly eight thousand soldiers now answer to him, but his belief in order has hardened into distrust of anyone who refuses his solution. House Storm's antiquity gives him pride, not a Valen claim. He has offered Mira marriage and threatened to march if she refuses. Southern people hear a conqueror; northern families hear the man who kept the passes open. The crisis may teach him that a defended kingdom is not the same thing as an obedient one.
allegiance: Military strength and administration, with no secure right to the crown.

name: Captain Garran Vale
summary: Owes his career to Ethan and his post to Mira. Honour has not offered him a clean order.

epilogue.loyal: Garran keeps the gate and sleeps badly, which is how he shows love.
epilogue.warm: Garran stays, though he will not toast either of his oaths.
epilogue.cold: Garran resigns the Guard and will not say whose name he failed.
epilogue.dead: The Guard cuts Garran's name into the roll and does not speak it at supper.
epilogue.missing: Garran leaves his sword on the table.
epilogue.captured: Without Garran the inner doors feel theoretical.

subtitle: Two Oaths, One Door
biography: Garran was the son of a Riverlands ferryman who died during a winter flood. The army offered regular meals; Ethan's company offered an education. Ethan taught him that the person behind a door mattered more than the lord who owned it. Mira later selected him to lead the forty-eight Queen's Guards, rewarding discipline rather than birth. He served her through losses and assassination rumours without asking to be loved. Ethan's exile left him obeying one sovereign household while doubting its account of another man. Garran refuses to turn an escort company into a squad of assassins. He will guard a ruler who keeps that distinction, even when the oath costs him an old friendship.
allegiance: Palace security; loyalty divided between Mira and Ethan.

name: Lady Celene Veyne
summary: Widowed, precise, and uninterested in who wears the crown so long as ships still move.

epilogue.loyal: Celene's tariffs arrive on time. Her warnings arrive earlier.
epilogue.warm: Celene keeps the ports open and her opinion shut.
epilogue.cold: Celene prices your reign the way she prices grain.
epilogue.dead: The coast does not mourn loudly. It raises prices.
epilogue.missing: Celene's captains say she is inspecting a warehouse. They smile.
epilogue.captured: Holding Celene is a good way to discover how fast a city can starve.

subtitle: The Tide's Accountant
biography: Celene learned trade in her father's harbour offices, where a lord's seal could delay a cargo and ruin three villages. Her husband died in a coastal storm eighteen years ago, leaving debts and captains who expected her to appoint a male steward. She cleared the debts herself. Veyne ships now carry salt, grain and letters through ports that would gladly feud if feuding paid. Celene sits on the Council of Nine and rarely declares an allegiance before she knows how it will feed a city. Her apparent indifference conceals a precise fear: a hungry capital can destroy the coast's warehouses as easily as an invading army. She bargains hard because the people who depend on her cannot eat a claimant's good intentions.
allegiance: Trade and food security; her support must survive the invoices.
public_biography: Celene learned trade in her father's harbour offices, where a lord's seal could delay a cargo and ruin three villages. name: Master Oren Pell
summary: He knows the illness and the last night. Erol made him swear, and Pell is the sort of man a swear sticks to.

epilogue.loyal: Pell remains at court and answers fewer questions than he is asked.
epilogue.warm: Pell will speak, a little, if the room is small.
epilogue.cold: Pell leaves the city with his notes burned.
epilogue.dead: The only physician who could have settled the death is dead himself.
epilogue.missing: Pell is no longer in the royal rooms.
epilogue.captured: Men are already inventing the confession they want from him.

subtitle: The Physician's Silence
biography: Oren Pell grew up above an apothecary and studied in the Flame's infirmaries before royal service took him to Caerlyn. He spent thirty years treating people who regarded their bodies as state property. Erol trusted him because he could speak plainly in private. When the king's hands weakened and his memory failed, Pell recorded the symptoms and obeyed an order to conceal them. On the final night he measured medicine, heard fragments of a testament, and was dismissed before dawn. His oath to Erol is real; so are the duties he owes the living. He fears that a careful clinical account will become whichever accusation a claimant can afford to print. Trust can move him. Threats can close the last reliable medical witness forever.
allegiance: Medical knowledge; an oath in conflict with public duty.
public_biography: Oren Pell trained in the Flame’s infirmaries before entering royal service. For thirty years he has treated a household accustomed to regarding its health as a matter of state. Erol valued his ability to speak plainly in private. The physician has refused a complete public account of the king’s final illness, citing a personal oath. Some courtiers call that loyalty; others call it concealment. Neither has persuaded him that a political audience can be trusted to preserve the limits of medical evidence.

name: Nessa Grey
summary: A former chamber servant who vanished after Erol's death. The court has rumours about her, but no account it can safely call her own.

epilogue.loyal: Nessa lives under a new name and still flinches at bells.
epilogue.warm: Nessa tells what she saw and then asks to be forgotten.
epilogue.cold: Nessa will not come to Caerlyn for any crown.
epilogue.dead: The last witness of the bedchamber is gone.
epilogue.missing: Nessa remains beyond the court’s reach. Rumours of the bedchamber continue, but the missing pieces remain hers.
epilogue.captured: Everyone wants Nessa. That is not the same as keeping her safe.

subtitle: The Witness Who Wants a Life
biography: Nessa's mother took in laundry below Caerlyn's Temple Quarter. A chamber post was supposed to pay for her younger brother's apprenticeship, not make her part of a succession crisis. Nessa learned to prepare a hearth, keep her eyes lowered and remember every instruction. On Erol's final night those habits became dangerous. She saw medicine carried, heard the end of a dictated document and fled when servants began disappearing from the household rolls. She has hidden among weavers along the River Vey. Nessa does not know every fact the court attributes to her. She wants her family safe and the right to give a limited account without having a confession invented around it.
allegiance: Her family's safety and the right to speak only for what she actually witnessed.
public_biography: Nessa’s mother takes in laundry below Caerlyn’s Temple Quarter. A chamber post was intended to pay for her younger brother’s apprenticeship. She prepared fires, carried linen and learned to remember instructions without drawing attention to herself. After Erol’s death she vanished from the household rolls. Rumours attribute more knowledge to her than anyone has confirmed. Finding Nessa will require discovering where an ordinary servant could obtain shelter, and why she would risk leaving it.

name: Marshal Bren Tal
summary: Twenty thousand soldiers swore to the Crown, not to a widow, a brother, a bastard, or a northern lord. Bren is keeping that sentence intact for as long as he can.

epilogue.loyal: Bren puts the royal army in the field under your banner and looks unhappy about the relief he feels.
epilogue.warm: Bren will fight for a settled monarch and not a moment sooner.
epilogue.cold: Bren keeps the army in camp and lets the claimants spend each other.
epilogue.dead: The royal army, suddenly leaderless, becomes everyone's argument.
epilogue.missing: Bren is not at the camp. The colonels are already choosing favourites.
epilogue.captured: The largest army in Nezrel is waiting to see who holds its marshal.

subtitle: The Army Between Names
biography: Bren began as a levy officer in the eastern war twenty years ago. He watched a noble feud waste soldiers just as Varos pressed the border, and has distrusted private armies ever since. Erol promoted him for keeping a retreat disciplined rather than disguising it as victory. As marshal he commands the royal establishment of roughly twenty thousand soldiers, dispersed across forts and garrisons. They swore to the Crown, not a claimant. Neutrality holds the army together, but each unpaid week makes it harder. Bren wants a lawful settlement, regular wages and prisoners treated as people. He can tolerate an imperfect sovereign. He will not willingly supply a civil war with the institution meant to end it.
allegiance: Professional command; law, pay, and restraint matter more than affection.

name: Lord Tomas Maren
summary: He raised Arlo and has never said why the royal purse paid for the privilege. He is afraid the truth will cost the boy.

epilogue.loyal: Tomas stands in public and looks older than he did in the stable yard.
epilogue.warm: Tomas sends horses and withholds the rest of the story.
epilogue.cold: Tomas closes the vale and calls it protection.
epilogue.dead: The man who could have explained the payments dies with them.
epilogue.missing: Tomas leaves the estate to Evelyne and a locked desk.
epilogue.captured: Tomas in chains makes Arlo someone's lever.

subtitle: The Cost of Keeping a Child
biography: Tomas inherited productive land rather than a glorious war record. He believes a good lord should be measured by next year's harvest. When Lysa died at the hunting lodge, he and Evelyne accepted her infant into Maren's household. Royal payments helped with the child's upkeep and purchased a silence Tomas has never been proud of. He gave Arlo education and work, but left him outside the register to avoid attracting Caerlyn's attention. Erol's secret visits gradually made that compromise impossible to defend. Tomas now faces the fact that protecting a child by concealment can become denying an adult his life. He will risk the house for Arlo; he hopes Arlo will not mistake that willingness for an unlimited treasury.
allegiance: Land, horses, and a father's protective compromise.

name: Lady Evelyne Maren
summary: Arlo's mother in every way that matters. She hated Erol for using her house as a cupboard.

epilogue.loyal: Evelyne comes to court and refuses to call it an honour.
epilogue.warm: Evelyne writes sharp letters and sends food.
epilogue.cold: Evelyne tells Arlo, or whoever is listening, that the vale was enough.
epilogue.dead: The vale's temper goes into the ground with her.
epilogue.missing: Evelyne will not be found in any hall that flies a Valen banner.
epilogue.captured: Evelyne does not bargain. Her captors discover this slowly.

subtitle: Mother Without a Writ
biography: Evelyne grew up on a border estate and learned to organise kitchens, stores and evacuation carts before she learned court etiquette. She lost a daughter to a childhood fever years before Arlo arrived. Taking in Lysa's son was a choice made with Tomas, not a service sold to a king. She raised him with the house's children, corrected his lessons and taught him to judge care by its work. Erol's visits angered her because he could enjoy the child without publicly protecting him. Evelyne is neither timid nor opposed to ambition. She opposes any future that asks Arlo to sacrifice the people who made him a person in order to prove who fathered him.
allegiance: Family, survival, and a refusal to let royal blood erase ordinary love.

name: Lord Edric Edevane
summary: Charming, ambitious, and already asking what happens to House Edevane if his aunt loses.

epilogue.loyal: Edric smiles in the correct rooms and remembers who put him there.
epilogue.warm: Edric is helpful. He is also counting.
epilogue.cold: Edric has already written the letter that abandons Mira. He has not sent it.
epilogue.dead: House Edevane's cleverest head is gone. The rest of them look smaller.
epilogue.missing: Edric is visiting friends. The friends are whoever is winning.
epilogue.captured: Edric talks enough to be dangerous and not enough to be useful.

subtitle: The Nephew with Two Drafts
biography: Edric's father died owing more than the Edevane estates could pay. Mira's influence rescued the house and gave her nephew his first place at court. He learned charm from ambassadors and finance from people who charged his family interest. At thirty-six he considers himself the architect of a future others are too sentimental to see. He supports his aunt in public, yet drafts assurances to possible victors in private. He fears the ruin of House Edevane almost as much as he desires an office worthy of his talents. An audited responsibility may make him useful. Humiliation may send him looking for someone who will mistake his ambition for loyalty.
allegiance: Court connections; real dependence mixed with dangerous ambition.

name: Father Aldren Veil
summary: He must light the Crown Candle. He is afraid of lighting it for someone who will burn the hearth down.

epilogue.loyal: Aldren lights the candle. His hand is not steady. The flame is.
epilogue.warm: Aldren prays for the realm and postpones the prayer for you.
epilogue.cold: Aldren will perform the rites and withhold the blessing that matters.
epilogue.dead: The Flame has no High Keeper, and every priest with ambition has noticed.
epilogue.missing: Aldren retreats into the temple and will not receive claimants.
epilogue.captured: A chained High Keeper makes a coronation look like a raid.

subtitle: Keeper of the Common Hearth
biography: Aldren entered a provincial shrine as a hungry apprentice and rose through the infirmaries and temple courts. At seventy-eight he remembers three coronations and more riots than he cares to count. The Flame teaches that every person bears a divine spark; a monarch keeps the hearth by preserving peace. Scripture does not prohibit a queen, although many provincial priests preach otherwise. Aldren knows the institution can survive a disputed rite more easily than it can survive blessing a ruler who burns villages. He is cautious because temples become hospitals when lords fail. He may accept political compromise, but cruelty presented as holiness tests the limits of his patience.
allegiance: Religious recognition; the Crown Candle is a duty, not a prize.

name: Lord Osric Harrow
summary: Poor, proud, and ready to bleed if it keeps House Storm out of the west.

epilogue.loyal: Osric brings longbows and an old grievance he expects you to share.
epilogue.warm: Osric fights your enemies and keeps his own accounts.
epilogue.cold: Osric remembers the old blood and not your name.
epilogue.dead: The west loses the lord who hated Storm most usefully.
epilogue.missing: Osric takes to the forest. The forest has always suited Harrow.
epilogue.captured: A Harrow in a Storm dungeon is a torch looking for a crowd.

subtitle: A House Living on Memory
biography: Osric grew up hearing that Harrow once chose kings. His own inheritance was wooded land, poor roads and tenants abandoning exhausted fields. House Storm's northern prosperity feels to him like a personal insult. He has kept a large western following through family names, skilled bowyers and concessions he cannot afford. His willingness to pay road bands to spare his villages has made his idea of protection dangerously selective. Osric can become a valuable ally against domination, or another lord who asks the kingdom to finance his grievance. Respect reaches him. Relief for his people reaches him more deeply than he likes to admit.
allegiance: Western levies and longbows; pride tied to a declining estate.

name: Chancellor Lucan Rook
summary: He believes a stable lie is kinder than a true civil war. He keeps the papers that can prove either.

epilogue.loyal: Lucan files your reign under the heading that will be hardest to appeal.
epilogue.warm: Lucan remains useful and slightly disappointed.
epilogue.cold: Lucan serves the office and waits to see if you survive it.
epilogue.dead: The archives lose their most careful liar.
epilogue.missing: Lucan is 'consulting records' in a room no one else can find.
epilogue.captured: Whoever holds the Chancellor holds the index to the kingdom.

subtitle: The Man Who Indexes Power
biography: Lucan was a copyist's son admitted to the royal archive after exposing a forged boundary writ. Erol discovered that his patience with documents exceeded his patience with people and made him Chancellor. Forty years later Lucan knows which customs are older than their legal justifications. He believes a stable compromise is often kinder than a civil war fought over perfect truth. That belief has also excused silences he would condemn in another man. He did not witness Erol's last hour; he can date and compare the papers that survived it. A ruler who demands honest procedure may give him a reason to recover his earlier principles.
allegiance: Law and records; capable of preserving a realm or legitimising its lies.
